description: PATCH /crm/businesses/:businessId/contacts/:contactId honours record visibility and business membership (R0-03 review ST-A high severity, ST-B should-fix). CrmService.updateContact applies the visibility clause GET detail applies (resolveCrmAccess + visibilityClause, the PR #190 semantics) in its access check and in its in-transaction read, so a contact the caller cannot see answers 404 byte-identical to an unknown id (timestamp and echoed path aside) with nothing written and no field of the row in the body; a visible contact the caller may not edit keeps its 403; a PATCH that changes ownerId is accepted only when the new owner holds a membership in the path business (the check reassignContacts applies, now shared as CrmService.assertNewOwnerIsMember), otherwise 400 with the bulk reassign message and nothing written ('' and unknown ids included), for HTTP and system-context callers; resending the current owner is not a change. Run from apps/server against a migrated local database and REDIS_URL: npx vitest run test/contacts-patch-visibility.integration.test.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-13c-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/contacts-patch-visibility.json --report .proof/r0-13c-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE on the unmodified source at 13b7389a (tests-first commit b090af9a): 11 of 20 fail, exactly the NEGATIVE CONTROL cases (ST-A: PATCH {} and PATCH {jobTitle} 200, a bundled reassignment 403, a crm_reassign takeover 200, a my-book edit 200, crm_edit owned 403 instead of 404; ST-B: another tenant's user, an unknown id, '' and a bundled outsider 200, the system-context call resolves). allowAdditionalCases is false: a change that adds, renames or removes a case in that suite must make the same change here. Review repairs (pkt/R0-13c-CT-PATCH-VISIBILITY-repair on 45ede9cf, 26 cases): ST-R1, updateContact locks the contact row (SELECT id FROM contacts ... FOR UPDATE) in its transaction before the in-transaction read, so a PATCH that resends the owner it read while a reassignment commits is decided on the committed row (403 without crm_reassign, the answer the same request gets afterwards) and cannot silently undo the reassignment, skip the membership check or be audited as 'updated'; ST-R2, softDeleteContact and bulkDeleteContacts apply the same visibility clause: DELETE of a contact the caller cannot see answers 404 byte-identical to an unknown id (not the delete-scope 403; an ADMIN-role member, who gets 404 on GET, no longer soft-deletes another member's PRIVATE contact) and bulk delete skips a hidden id exactly like a missing one, while a visible contact outside crm_delete 'owned' keeps its 403. RED-BEFORE on 45ede9cf: exactly the 4 new NEGATIVE CONTROL cases fail (race 200 with owner_id restored to the departed owner, staff DELETE 403, ADMIN DELETE 200, bulk {deleted:1}); the 2 other new cases and the 20 earlier ones pass. R0-13d-CT-BULK-ENRICH-VISIBILITY (pkt/R0-13d-CT-BULK-ENRICH-VISIBILITY on e9391eda, 39 cases): bulk update and enrichment, the remaining member-facing contact write paths, apply the same visibility clause. CrmService.bulkUpdateContacts selects the editable rows through editableContactClause (visibilityClause plus the edit scope, both reused), so a hidden id is skipped and counted exactly like a missing one and gets no write, event or audit entry. ContactEnrichmentService takes its edit decision from CrmService.assertCanEditContact, the check updateContact now calls (extracted from it, CR-1), before it reads the row, calls the provider or stamps custom.enrichment, so POST contacts/:id/enrich on a contact the caller cannot see answers 404 byte-identical to an unknown id with no provider call (the enrichment provider is a recording stub injected for ApolloEnrichmentProvider; no real provider is ever called). CR-3: a PATCH (and a system updateContact) naming a non-member owner answers 400 'ownerId must belong to a member of this business', the field the PATCH body has (bulk reassign keeps 'newOwnerId ...'), and createContact uses the shared assertNewOwnerIsMember helper; one case renamed accordingly. PATCH contacts/bulk is declared after PATCH contacts/:contactId in crm.controller.ts and is answered by it today (404 for id 'bulk', M15, V1-54 owns the controller), so the bulk cases drive the real CrmService exactly as CrmController.bulkUpdateContacts forwards a member's request, and one HTTP case proves the route answers a hidden id byte-identically to an unknown one whichever handler it reaches. RED-BEFORE on e9391eda (tests-first commit bd0c5063): 11 of 39 fail: 3 bulk NEGATIVE CONTROL (a crm 'write' STAFF member's update of another member's PRIVATE contact answers {updated:1} where an unknown id is 403, next to a TEAM contact {updated:2}, a 'my book' member updates another member's TEAM contact), 4 enrichment NEGATIVE CONTROL (201 no_match and a stamp on the hidden contact, a forced match sends its email and name to the provider before the 404, a 'my book' member 201, a crm_edit 'owned' member 403 instead of 404) and the 4 PATCH/system member-message cases ('newOwnerId ...'); the 28 others pass. GREEN-AFTER: 39 of 39. R0-13d review repairs (pkt/R0-13d-CT-BULK-ENRICH-VISIBILITY-repair on 16a06728, 41 cases): ST-1, bulkUpdateContacts selects the rows it writes through the tenant predicate for every caller (the owner, a super admin and a call with no actor, the KEY flow-orchestrator 'update_status_with_confirmation' tool, included; a limited member additionally through editableContactClause), writes them with updateManyAndReturn under the same scope, and records an event and, after commit, an audit entry only for the rows it wrote, so another tenant's id is skipped exactly like an unknown id (the same count, no ContactEvent or ContactAuditEntry under either tenant) and an unknown id no longer fails the contact_events foreign key after an orphan audit entry was written; ST-2, a member's bulk update is recorded as that member (memberAuditContext, as updateContact): the bulk_updated audit entries name them as USER and the bulk.updated events carry actorType USER and their id, while a call with no actor stays SYSTEM. RED-BEFORE on 16a06728: exactly the 2 new NEGATIVE CONTROL cases fail (the owner's unknown id 500 from contactEvent.create where another tenant's id answers {updated:0}; the staff member's audit actor {type: SYSTEM}); the 39 others pass. GREEN-AFTER: 41 of 41.
